pages.text: The Turning-Light Trail
pages.alt: Mia, Sol, Tavi and Vee stand on a moonlit garden path leading to the Sunrise Arch. Stable moon and sun emoji cards mark the trail.

pages.heading: A Star Rooms adventure
pages.text: Mia, Sol and Tavi follow two lights through a moonlit garden. Can you help them turn, return, find a broken step and wake the Sunrise Arch?
pages.subtext:
Written by Maria Smith
Book 3 of 4 · ages 3–5 · review edition 2.0.0

This is a live review copy, not an approved final publication.
pages.alt: A moon emoji, a sun emoji and a turning arrow introduce the book's journey.

pages.heading: The lantern begins
pages.text:
Last time, Mia, Sol and Tavi carried every part of the Moon Lantern and rebuilt the same whole.

Now the lantern glowed: moon, sun, moon.
pages.alt: The friends watch the same complete lantern. Stable moon, sun and moon emoji cards show its three lights.

pages.heading: The light runs away
pages.text:
The three lights skipped into the garden. Then the next path stone stayed dark.

Far ahead, the Sunrise Arch was still asleep.
pages.alt: Moon, sun and moon emoji cards lead to one clearly dark path stone. The Sunrise Arch waits in the distance.

pages.heading: Meet Vee
pages.text:
A purple path keeper hurried over.

“I’m Vee. This trail should wake the Sunrise Arch. Will you help us find the rule and mend the dark path?”
pages.alt: Vee joins Mia, Sol and Tavi beside the stopped trail. The dark stone and distant arch keep the mission visible.

pages.heading: One tile, two sides
pages.text:
Vee lifted one thick trail tile. One side showed a moon. The other side showed a sun.

It was one tile with two different sides.
pages.alt: Two views of the same tile sit side by side: one has the stable moon emoji and one has the stable sun emoji.

pages.heading: What is showing?
pages.text:
Look at Vee’s tile. Only one side faces up.

Point to the picture you can see now: MOON or SUN.
pages.subtext: Make your choice. The next page shows the answer.
pages.alt: A large tile shows the moon side. Separate moon and sun emoji answer cards appear below it.

pages.heading: The moon side is showing
pages.text:
The moon is showing because we can see it now.

The sun is underneath. It is still part of the same tile, even though we cannot see it from above.
pages.alt: The moon emoji is labelled SHOWING. A dim sun emoji below it is labelled UNDERNEATH.

pages.heading: The first gate
pages.text:
Mia slid the tile into a round gate with the moon facing up.

Sol pulled the handle once. The gate turned the tile all the way over.
pages.alt: A moon-side tile enters the round turning gate. One clear curved arrow shows one complete turn.

pages.heading: Turn once
pages.text:
Hold one hand flat with your palm up. Turn it over once.

The tile began with MOON showing. Which side will show after one turn?
pages.subtext: Point to MOON or SUN. Then turn the page.
pages.alt: A moon card, one turning arrow and an empty after-card appear above moon and sun answer choices.

pages.heading: One turn shows the sun
pages.text:
The sun now faces up. It is still the same tile.

A turn is the one agreed move that changes which side we can see.
pages.alt: A before card shows moon. An arrow marked ONE TURN leads to an after card showing sun.

pages.heading: Turn once more
pages.text:
The sun faces up now. Turn your hand over once more.

Which side will show next?
pages.subtext: Point to MOON or SUN. The answer is on the next page.
pages.alt: A sun card, one turning arrow and an empty after-card appear above moon and sun answer choices.

pages.heading: The moon returns
pages.text:
The moon faces up again. It showed first, went underneath, and came back.

Return means an earlier side is showing again.
pages.alt: A sun before-card turns into a moon after-card. The moon card is labelled RETURNS.

pages.heading: Turn, then return
pages.text:
Start with moon. One turn shows sun. The next turn brings moon back.

We call this a Fold rule: turn to the other side, then return to the first.
pages.alt: Three stable emoji cards show moon, sun and moon, joined by two one-turn arrows.

pages.heading: Follow the lights
pages.text:
Point from left to right. Say each picture:

MOON · SUN · MOON · SUN
pages.subtext: What do you notice about the order?
pages.alt: Four large emoji cards form a row: moon, sun, moon, sun.

pages.heading: What comes next?
pages.text:
MOON · SUN · MOON · SUN · ?

The same order is starting again. Which picture belongs in the empty place?
pages.subtext: Point to MOON or SUN. Check on the next page.
pages.alt: Moon, sun, moon and sun emoji cards are followed by one white blank card. Moon and sun choices appear below.

pages.heading: Moon comes next
pages.text:
Moon comes next because the order starts again: moon, sun, moon, sun, moon.

A pattern is an order that repeats. The Fold’s turn-and-return rule made this pattern.
pages.alt: The empty place is filled by the stable moon emoji. The full repeated row is visible.

pages.heading: Sol tries a tile
pages.text:
The lights moved farther. Sol placed the next tile with its moon side up.

Now the row said moon, sun, moon, moon. The trail stopped again.
pages.alt: The visible row is moon, sun, moon, moon. Sol's last moon card stays visible at the stopped trail.

pages.heading: Find the first break
pages.text:
Check the row from left to right:

MOON · SUN · MOON · MOON

Which card is the first one that does not follow the moon-sun order?
pages.subtext: Touch each card once. Point to the first break.
pages.alt: Four numbered emoji cards show moon, sun, moon, moon. No answer is marked.

pages.heading: The fourth card breaks the rule
pages.text:
The fourth card is the first break. After moon, the rule needs sun. Sol’s card shows moon instead.

We kept the first try so we could compare it.
pages.alt: The fourth moon card is ringed and labelled FIRST BREAK. A sun card beside it is labelled THE RULE NEEDS SUN.

pages.heading: The trail moves again
pages.text:
Sol kept a little picture of his first try. Then he turned the fourth tile to sun.

Moon, sun, moon, sun! The repaired trail glowed.
pages.alt: A small inset keeps the original moon-sun-moon-moon row. The main row shows the repaired moon-sun-moon-sun sequence.

pages.heading: Two ways across
pages.text:
The light reached a bridge. One beam travelled over the bridge. The next travelled under it.

The pictures changed, but two ways could still take turns.
pages.alt: One labelled route goes over the bridge and another labelled route goes under it.

pages.heading: Which way comes next?
pages.text:
OVER · UNDER · OVER · ?

Point to the way that keeps the same take-turns rule.
pages.subtext: Choose OVER or UNDER. The next page reveals it.
pages.alt: Three labelled route cards show over, under and over, followed by one blank card. Over and under choices are separate.

pages.heading: Under comes next
pages.text:
Over, under, over, under. UNDER comes next.

The names changed, but the two-part take-turns rule stayed the same.
pages.alt: Four labelled route cards show over, under, over, under across the bridge.

pages.heading: Three paths to the arch
pages.text:
Three paths waited beyond the bridge.

The friends needed one path that reached the Sunrise Arch and kept moon and sun taking turns all the way.
pages.alt: Three clearly separated paths are labelled A, B and C. Each uses the same stable moon and sun emoji cards.

pages.heading: Choose the complete path
pages.text:
Check every path.

Does it reach the arch? Do moon and sun take turns all the way?

Point to A, B or C.
pages.subtext: The next page keeps all three paths visible and explains the answer.
pages.alt: Path A stops early. Path B reaches the arch but repeats sun. Path C reaches the arch and alternates moon and sun.

pages.heading: Path C does both jobs
pages.text:
Path C reaches the arch, and every light follows the rule.

Path A stops early. Path B breaks the order. Keeping all three helps us compare.
pages.alt: Path C is outlined in gold while paths A and B remain visible with their different problems.

pages.heading: Remember the first gate
pages.text:
A moon-side tile entered the first gate. The gate turned it once.

Which side came out?
pages.subtext: Use what you remember. Choose MOON or SUN.
pages.alt: A moon card enters a turning gate. The after-card is blank. Moon and sun choices appear below.

pages.heading: Sun came out
pages.text:
Sun came out after one turn. You brought an earlier result back to mind.

Remembering helps us use what we have already learned.
pages.alt: A before card shows moon and an after card shows sun, joined by one turn arrow.

pages.heading: New pictures, same rule
pages.text:
STAR · LEAF · STAR · ?

The pictures are new. Which one keeps the same take-turns rule?
pages.subtext: Point to STAR or LEAF. Then turn the page.
pages.alt: Star, leaf and star emoji cards are followed by one blank card. Star and leaf choices appear below.

pages.heading: Leaf comes next
pages.text:
Star, leaf, star, leaf. LEAF comes next.

The pictures changed, but the same two-part rule still worked. The Sunrise Arch shone!
pages.alt: The complete star-leaf-star-leaf emoji row glows beneath the Sunrise Arch as the four friends celebrate.

pages.heading: You mended the trail
pages.text:
You found two different sides and one clear move between them. One turn showed the other side. The next turn brought the first side back.

Repeating that move made a pattern. You used the rule to predict, find a break and repair the path. A clear rule helps us know what should come next and check when something changes.

At the garden gate, Tavi asked, “How can we check our work?”

pages.alt: The Sunrise Arch glows. Mia, Sol, Tavi and Vee wave beside the repaired path. A garden gate ahead teases the next book.
